worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\,\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta )=1-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ ${\theta }_{1}=0,$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\pi $, this gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\frac{1}{2}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(\frac{3}{2}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{3}{2}\theta -2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )}{4}){|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{3}{2}\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )}{4}\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }\,) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )}{8}\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{3}{4}(\pi -0)-(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))+\frac{1}{8}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}-0+0 \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
